body.statement: Under overlap, bounded outcomes, bounded aspect ratio, propensity-path stability, the primitive oracle gap, and \(b_{nm}=o(1)\), \(Z^{\mathrm B}=Z^{\bar p}+D^{\mathrm B}+R^{\mathrm B}\), where \(E_P[Z^{\bar p}_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]=M^{\mathrm B}_{ij}\). The residual \(R^{\mathrm B}\), which contains the centered linear derivative and the quadratic ratio term, contributes \(o_P(b_{nm})\) to normalized maximum-row subspace loss, and \(\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},U^{\mathrm B})=O_P(b_{nm})\).
body.justification: This exhibits the empirical denominator as a leading object rather than hiding it in a remainder.
body.gap: Khan and Ugander's published Theorem 3 and equation (10) on page 7 analyze a scalar affine normalizer under independent treatment indicators, not a same-path row ratio inside an SVD; their Discussion on page 18 lists dependent indicators as an open extension.
body.consumer: It audits legacy mobile-health data retaining treatment counts but not decision probabilities.
